title: I Said I’d Decide After Earnings. Here’s What I’m Doing With SoFi
creator: Couch Investor
summary: Couch Investor delivers the decision he promised before earnings: what he will do with SoFi, already a quite big position, after its third quarter. He says SoFi beat across the board and the stock was up about 13% at the time of recording, trading around $16–$16.40. Revenue grew 44% year over year, adjusted EBITDA was $470 million at a 34% margin, adjusted net income was $243 million, and originations hit a record $16.9 billion, up 71%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 40% revenue growth and gave a 2027 outlook of revenue up 27%, an adjusted EBITDA margin of 35% and adjusted EPS of $0.90, funded without raising capital; segment guidance has lending up 25% in 2027, the tech platform up 25% and financial services up 35% or more. He argues SoFi historically beats and raises its own targets, so 2028 EPS could reach about $1.30 against a target range around $1.12 if the macro backdrop improves. His cautions are macro: the guidance assumes up to two more rate hikes in 2026 and two in 2027, and a fourth-quarter lending dip and credit-card losses were not explained on the call. He calls the stock undervalued and cheap on his free DCF model. The call is SOFI — BUY, a stance flip from CONDITIONAL_BUY on 26 October, the pre-earnings condition having been met.
